title: The Secret to Soft and Hydrated Lips

content.text: The Secret to Soft and Hydrated Lips

Soft, comfortable lips rarely need a complicated routine. A few gentle habits can help protect them from dryness and keep them feeling smooth through changing weather, long days and every lipstick moment in between.
Start with a simple, gentle routine

The skin on your lips is delicate, so keep cleansing and exfoliating light. At the end of the day, remove lipstick gently with a soft cloth or a suitable cleanser. If your lips feel flaky, resist picking or scrubbing them; irritation can make them feel even more uncomfortable.
Choose a balm that locks in moisture

Look for a fragrance-free lip balm with nourishing, protective ingredients such as petrolatum, shea butter or ceramides. Apply it whenever your lips feel dry, and add a generous layer before bed. Reapplying regularly helps maintain a comfortable barrier, especially in cold, windy or dry conditions.
Give your lips daily sun protection

Lips can be exposed to the sun just like the rest of your face. During the day, use a lip balm with broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher and reapply according to the product directions, particularly after eating, drinking or swimming.
Notice what leaves them feeling dry

Licking your lips may feel soothing for a moment, but saliva evaporates quickly and can leave them feeling drier. Some plumping products, strong flavours or fragranced formulas can also bother sensitive lips. If a product stings or makes your lips feel worse, stop using it and switch to a gentle, fragrance-free balm.

For a smoother lipstick finish, apply balm while you get ready and blot away any excess just before adding colour. A creamy lipstick or tinted balm can feel more comfortable than a very matte formula when your lips are dry. Keep a familiar balm close by for touch-ups throughout the day.

Soft lips are usually the result of gentle care repeated often, not a harsh overnight fix. Keep your routine uncomplicated: protect your lips in the daytime, replenish them when they feel dry and give them a comfortable layer before sleep. If dryness is persistent, painful or cracked, consider checking in with a healthcare professional.
